# About the Author {.unnumbered}

Vijay Janapa Reddi is the Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering at
Harvard University. His research spans computer architecture, runtime systems,
edge computing, and machine-learning systems, with a longstanding focus on
co-design across hardware, software, systems, and machine learning. He is
particularly interested in problems at these intersections, where progress
often depends on connecting decisions that are usually studied one layer at a
time.

Measurement is a second recurring thread. As a founding board member of
MLCommons and an early co-chair of MLPerf Inference, he has helped make
machine-learning performance claims measurable and reproducible.

Architecture 2.0 brings these threads together. It treats AI-assisted system
and chip design as a cross-layer engineering problem and asks how new methods
can improve the resulting system in ways that can be measured, checked, and
reproduced.
